results.name: Airy Labs
results.what_happened: Airy Labs was an educational gaming startup that raised $1.5 million from Google Ventures, Foundation Capital, and others. Within a year, the company laid off the vast majority of its ~20-person staff, leaving only a skeleton crew. Former employees blamed management issues, including allegations that Hsu's father was secretly running the company. Airy Labs effectively shut down.

results.name: Cambrian Genomics
results.what_happened: Cambrian Genomics developed "laser-printed DNA" technology and raised $10 million in venture funding. The company faced intense controversy over ethical concerns about its synthetic biology ambitions. Negative press damaged its ability to raise further capital. Founder Austen Heinz died by suicide in May 2015, and the company ceased operations.

results.name: Luminar Technologies (LAZR)
results.what_happened: Luminar, a lidar technology company for self-driving cars, went public via SPAC in 2020 at a $3.4 billion valuation, briefly making Russell the world's youngest self-made billionaire. The company's market cap subsequently collapsed to roughly $179 million. In 2024, Luminar cut 30% of its workforce (212 employees). In May 2025, founder Austin Russell resigned as CEO following a board ethics inquiry, and another round of layoffs began. Volvo terminated its contract with Luminar. The company ultimately filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and is seeking an asset sale.

results.name: GigLocator
results.what_happened: GigLocator, a service for finding concert tickets based on user interests, was the Thiel Fellowship's first "exit" — sold to Brooklyn Bowl in 2012. While Proud said he was "satisfied," the sale price was not disclosed and was widely considered a very modest outcome rather than a significant success. Proud moved on to other ventures.

results.name: Volley AI
results.what_happened: Volley AI was described as a "first generation large language model startup" serving Fortune 500 companies. The company appears to have wound down, with Admani moving on to co-found 305 Ventures, a venture capital fund.
